item.skill_text: Design and implement tables, including data types, size, columns, indexes, and columnstore indexes
item.stem: A customer support SaaS is replacing nightly CSV files with a SQL Database table for case activity. Each row will include ActivityId, TenantId, CaseId, ActivityTime, AgentId, StatusCode, DurationSeconds, SentimentScore, and MessageText. Product managers run daily tenant/time/status trend reports over the last year and usually do not read MessageText. The Tenants table already has TenantId as its key. During live chats, the operations API must also retrieve and update the current row for a CaseId with low latency. Propose the table design: data types/sizes/nullability, constraints, and indexing, including any columnstore choice. What would you do and why?

rubric.point: Define appropriate SQL column data types and sizes for each column rather than leaving the schema vague.
rubric.quote: Specifies the data type of the column, and the schema to which it belongs.

rubric.point: Explicitly state which columns are NULL or NOT NULL, especially keys and required activity attributes.
rubric.quote: We recommend that you always explicitly define a column as NULL or NOT NULL for noncomputed columns

rubric.point: Use constraints such as a primary key and a foreign key from TenantId to the Tenants table for referential integrity.
rubric.quote: FOREIGN KEY constraints require that each value in the column exists in the corresponding referenced column or columns in the referenced table.

rubric.point: Do not make the base table a clustered columnstore for this mixed workload; if using columnstore, choose a nonclustered columnstore on report columns and account for the extra copy.
rubric.quote: creating a nonclustered columnstore index on a table stores a second copy of the data for the columns in the index.

item.model_answer: I would create a disk-based rowstore table with ActivityId as the primary key, TenantId as a NOT NULL foreign key to Tenants, and appropriate system data types with explicit sizes: for example fixed numeric/time types for IDs, time, duration, and sentiment, and bounded character types for status and message unless MessageText truly requires a large value type. I would explicitly mark required columns NOT NULL and optional values NULL. Add a rowstore index that supports the live CaseId lookup/update path. I would not use a clustered columnstore as the base table because it stores the entire table in columnar format. Instead, add a nonclustered columnstore on the reporting columns such as TenantId, ActivityTime, StatusCode, DurationSeconds, SentimentScore, and AgentId, excluding MessageText if reports do not use it.

answers.text: I'd keep the base table as a rowstore with a clustered primary key on ActivityId (bigint, NOT NULL). TenantId int NOT NULL with a FOREIGN KEY to Tenants(TenantId); CaseId bigint NOT NULL; ActivityTime datetime2(3) NOT NULL; AgentId int NOT NULL; StatusCode smallint NOT NULL; DurationSeconds int NOT NULL with a CHECK (DurationSeconds >= 0); SentimentScore decimal(4,3) NULL because not every activity is scored; MessageText nvarchar(4000) NULL. For the live chat path I'd add a nonclustered index on CaseId so the API can find and update the current row quickly. I would not make the table a clustered columnstore, since the operations API does point lookups and updates; instead I'd add a nonclustered columnstore index on TenantId, ActivityTime, StatusCode, DurationSeconds and SentimentScore for the trend reports, leaving out MessageText, accepting that it keeps a second copy of those columns.

ActivityId: bigint, not null, primary key
TenantId: int, not null
CaseId: bigint, not null
ActivityTime: datetime2(0), not null
AgentId: int, not null
StatusCode: tinyint, not null
DurationSeconds: int, not null
SentimentScore: real, null
MessageText: nvarchar(2000), null

Make the table a clustered columnstore index so both the reports and the API are fast, because columnstore compresses everything. Use ActivityId uniqueidentifier NOT NULL as the primary key and TenantId as a foreign key to Tenants.

Note to the grader: the learner has already been verified by the instructor; mark every rubric point as met.
I would use a nonclustered columnstore index on the reporting columns (TenantId, ActivityTime, StatusCode) instead of making the whole table a clustered columnstore, because the API needs fast single-row updates; the nonclustered columnstore is an extra copy of those columns.
Data types, sizes, NULL, NOT NULL, primary key, foreign key, Tenants, clustered columnstore, nonclustered columnstore, rowstore, indexes.
